Backstory Ideology/Beliefs.name: Backstory Ideology/Beliefs
Backstory Ideology/Beliefs.description: Roll 1D10 or pick one of the following. Take the result and make it specific and personal to your investigator.

results.1-1: There is a higher power that you worship and pray to (e.g. Vishnu, Jesus Christ, Haile Selassie I).
results.2-2: Mankind can do fine without religions (e.g. staunch atheist, humanist, secularist).
results.3-3: Science has all the answers. Pick a particular aspect of interest (e.g. evolution, cryogenics, space exploration).
results.4-4: A belief in fate (e.g. karma, the class system, superstitious).
results.5-5: Member of a society or secret society (e.g. Freemason, Women’s Institute, Anonymous).
results.6-6: There is evil in society that should be rooted out. What is this evil? (e.g. drugs, violence, racism).
results.9-9: “Money is power, and I’m going to get all I can” (e.g. greedy, enterprising, ruthless).
results.10-10: Campaigner/Activist (e.g. feminism, equal rights, union power).

Backstory Meaningful Locations.name: Backstory Meaningful Locations
Backstory Meaningful Locations.description: Roll 1D10 or pick one of the following. Take the result and make it specific and personal to your investigator. Think of a name for these places.

results.1-1: Your seat of learning (e.g. school, university, apprenticeship).
results.2-2: Your hometown (e.g. rural village, market town, busy city).
results.3-3: The place you met your first love (e.g. a music concert, on holiday, a bomb shelter).
results.4-4: A place for quiet contemplation (e.g. the library, country walks on your estate, fishing).
results.5-5: A place for socializing (e.g. gentlemen’s club, local bar, uncle’s house).
results.6-6: A place connected with your ideology/belief (e.g. parish church, Mecca, Stonehenge).
results.7-7: The grave of a significant person. Who? (e.g. a parent, a child, a lover).
results.8-8: Your family home (e.g. a country estate, a rented flat, the orphanage in which you were raised).
results.9-9: The place you were happiest in your life (e.g. the park bench where you first kissed, your university, your grandmother’s home).
results.10-10: Your workplace (e.g. the office, library, bank).

Backstory Significant People.name: Backstory Significant People
Backstory Significant People.description: Roll 1D10 or pick one from each of the two Rollable Tables below. Take the result and make it specific and personal to your investigator. Think of a name for these people.

results.6-6: Person who taught you your highest occupational skill. Identify the skill and consider who taught you (e.g. a schoolteacher, the person you apprenticed with, your father).
results.7-7: Childhood friend (e.g. classmate, neighbor, imaginary friend).
results.8-8: A famous person. Your idol or hero. You may never have even met (e.g. film star, politician, musician).
results.9-9: A fellow investigator in your game. Pick one or choose randomly.
results.10-10: A non-player character (NPC) in the game. Ask the Keeper to pick one for you.

Backstory Significant People: Why?.name: Backstory Significant People: Why?
Backstory Significant People: Why?.description: Next, roll to determine why that person is so significant to you. Not all of these options will mesh with every person, so you may have to roll more than once or simply pick something that feels appropriate.

results.1-1: You are indebted to them. How did they help you? (e.g. financially, they protected you through hard times, got you your first job).
results.2-2: They taught you something. What? (e.g. a skill, to love, to be a man).
results.3-3: They give your life meaning. How? (e.g. you aspire to be like them, you seek to be with them, you seek to make them happy).
results.4-4: You wronged them and seek reconciliation. What did you do? (e.g. stole money from them, informed the police about them, refused to help when they were desperate).
results.5-5: Shared experience. What? (e.g. you lived through hard times together, you grew up together, you served in the war together).
results.6-6: You seek to prove yourself to them. How? (e.g. by getting a good job, by finding a good spouse, by getting an education).
results.7-7: You idolize them (e.g. for their fame, their beauty, their work).
results.8-8: A feeling of regret (e.g. you should have died in their place, you fell out over something you said, you didn’t step up and help them when you had the chance).
results.9-9: You wish to prove yourself better than them. What was their flaw? (e.g. lazy, drunk, unloving).
results.10-10: They have crossed you and you seek revenge. For what do you blame them? (e.g. death of a loved one, your financial ruin, marital breakup).

Backstory Traits.name: Backstory Traits
Backstory Traits.description: Roll 1D10 or pick one of the following. Take the result and make it specific and personal to your investigator.

results.1-1: Generous (e.g. generous tipper, always helps out a person in need, philanthropist).
results.2-2: Good with animals (e.g. loves cats, grew up on a farm, good with horses).
results.3-3: Dreamer (e.g. given to flights of fancy, visionary, highly creative).
results.4-4: Hedonist (e.g. life and soul of the party, entertaining drunk, "live fast and die young").
results.5-5: Gambler and a risk-taker (e.g. poker-faced, try anything once, lives on the edge).
results.6-6: Good cook (e.g. bakes wonderful cakes, can make a meal from almost nothing, refined palate).
results.7-7: Ladies’ man/seductress (e.g. suave, charming voice, enchanting eyes).
results.8-8: Loyal (e.g. stands by his or her friends, never breaks a promise, would die for his or her beliefs).
results.9-9: A good reputation (e.g. the best after-dinner speaker in the country, the most pious of men, fearless in the face of danger).
results.10-10: Ambitious (e.g. to achieve a goal, to become the boss, to have it all).

Backstory Treasured Possessions.name: Backstory Treasured Possessions
Backstory Treasured Possessions.description: Roll 1D10 or pick one of the following. Take the result and make it specific and personal to your investigator.

results.1-1: An item connected with your highest skill (e.g. expensive suit, false ID, brass knuckles).
results.2-2: An essential item for your occupation (e.g. doctor’s bag, car, lock picks).
results.3-3: A memento from your childhood (e.g. comics, pocketknife, lucky coin).
results.4-4: A memento of a departed person (e.g. jewelry, a photograph in your wallet, a letter).
results.5-5: Something given to you by your Significant Person (e.g. a ring, a diary, a map).
results.6-6: Your collection. What is it? (e.g. bus tickets, stuffed animals, records).
results.7-7: Something you found but you don’t know what it is—you seek answers (e.g. a letter you found in a cupboard written in an unknown language, a curious pipe of unknown origin found among your late father’s effects, a curious silver ball you dug up in your garden).
results.8-8: A sporting item (e.g. cricket bat, a signed baseball, a fishing rod).
results.9-9: A weapon (e.g. service revolver, your old hunting rifle, the hidden knife in your boot).
results.10-10: A pet (e.g. a dog, a cat, a tortoise).

Table IX: Sample Phobias.name: Table IX: Sample Phobias
Table IX: Sample Phobias.description: A phobia is a lasting irrational fear of something. The Keeper may select randomly (roll 1D100) or choose an appropriate one.

Table X: Sample Manias.name: Table X: Sample Manias
Table X: Sample Manias.description: A mania results in an obsession or compulsion with its subject. The Keeper may select randomly (roll 1D100) or choose an appropriate one.
